Paul Edwards continued the busy schedule of competitions that seems to see him in a different country every week. He had no trouble in disposing of the domestic shot opposition, and Abi Ekoku saw off the other discus men, although he was pressed by a 19 year old who held the lead until Abi launched…
Paul Edwards, sporting his new tailor made 56 inch Belgrave vest, ignored the conditions to heave the shot 19.18 metres, while Abi settled for 2nd spot in the 'B'.

The IAAF Grand Prix season kicked off in Sao Paulo, Brazil, on May 17th and Paul Edwards did well in exalted company to place 3rd with 19.87, close up to the two leading Americans and ahead of the Swede Larsson who was 7th in the 1991 World Champs.

Take last season, when Paul Edwards' quest for the perfect putt took him to Tokyo (Japan), Gainesville (USA), Oristana and Turin (Italy), Vladimir (Russia), Frankfurt (Germany), Seville (Spain), Zurich (Switzerland), Oslo (Norway), Paris (France) and Limerick (Ireland).

Dreams do not always come true, however, and it was a bitterly disappointed Belgravian who could only place 14th in his pool with 5.20m, failing at 5.30m. Paul Edwards - Shot Putt On his best form, a place in the top six beckoned.

Olympic champion Mike Stulce of the US again got the best of the world's top shot putters with a 21.34 effort while Paul Edwards had a sequence of foul, 17.57, 18.40, 17.95, 18.61, foul, to take 5th place.
As usual Paul Edwards had far too much muscle for his domestic opposition but was in turn well beaten by the three Americans with Olympic Champion Stulce setting an all-comers record of 21.77.

Then came the throwers with Paul Edwards on 94 and Abi Ekoku on 87.75. Well, we've missed those two injured men Jon and Lewis badly and in the mean time the throwers have strengthened their hold on the points table, taking over positions 1, 2 and 4.
His 19.16m was within reach of a Paul Edwards at his very best but while the Briton went a little further with each throw, so too did the Italian.

Paul Edwards broke Mike Edwards record of consecutive league wins by asserting his superiority in all of the shot competitions. But the revelation was Leith Marar who was in his first full year competing in our 'A' squad.
Leith Marar made a big impact in the throws while Paul Edwards insisted on adding the pole vault to his repertoire (Ok, he was a decathlete) and gained 4th in the 'B' vault.
Kasse Tadesse, Paul Edwards and Leith Marar repeated their first match wins with Paul again covering gaps, this time the 'B' javelin. Ian Tullett won the pole vault as Mike Edwards no-heighted.
Leith Marar took the opportunity to score yet more points, adding the hammer to the discus and shot, which Paul Edwards (back from Edinburgh) again won easily.

We thought that we had made a good start what with Phil Spivey's second place in the hammer, John Mackenzie gaining second in his only long jump in the season, Kasse winning the 10,000m running the second half in 14:26, followed by Paul Edwards' victory in the shot.

Not at all happy either with his day's work was Paul Edwards who only allowed two of his efforts to be measured and Gary Staines' confidence also took a knock in the 10k as he barely cracked the half-hour.

Paul Edwards missed out on a berth in the final by just 10cm as he hit 18.54m. Ukrainian Aleksandr Klimenko won at 20.78m with two others from his country making it a clean sweep for the Eastern European plainsmen.

Mike Edwards opened at 5.20 and went clear at his first attempt to share the lead but a handful of men were also successful at subsequent attempts and ominously the outstanding favourite from South Africa, Okert Brits, and the Aussie Miller had yet to come in.

Lewis Samuel doubled up in the 'B' 200 due to Lennie Paul's non-appearance and concluded an excellent afternoon with a 47.38 split in the long relay. The throws were once again our saviour led by Paul Edwards.
